rationale: Re-deriving a line break inside a box that the break itself determined is not reliable at any metric quality. An auto-width label's box was sized BY its own text, so it has no slack, and any positive epsilon in a measured advance pushes the last word onto a second line; Pulp measures a captured string about 0.65% wider than the browser's own line box for reasons not yet explained. Label therefore gains an optional CACHE of a browser's line breaking — rects plus UTF-16 offsets — used verbatim while the conditions that produced it still hold, and discarded for a normal reflow the moment they do not. The node stays one semantic paragraph, so accessibility, selection, translation and edit addressing are unaffected and reflow remains available; this is the same measure-once-reflow-forever shape PreparedText already implements, with the expensive measurement arriving from outside. Invalidation is deliberately conservative: the resolved face identity (a PostScript name, not the requested family, since one family covers several instances that break differently), the container width the text was broken at, and the text content itself; anything unknown counts as a mismatch, because a wrongly reused cache reintroduces the defect while a wrongly discarded one costs only a reflow. FontResolver gains resolved_face_identity so a caller outside the canvas can ask which instance a family stack resolves to without reaching for Skia types. Measured against Chrome on the design corpus, delay improves 0.1020 to 0.0965 area-weighted failing at unchanged 100% ink coverage. Pulp-only: the defect and the fix both originate here, with no counterpart framework change to backport.
